question_text:
Complete the following reaction sequence and give the name of major product 'P'.
$CH_3-CH_2-C\equiv N \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } H_3O^+]{\text{(i) } OH^-/H_2O/\Delta} \xrightarrow[\text{(iv) } H_2O]{\text{(iii) } Cl_2/\text{Red P}} P \text{ (Major product)}$
solution_text:
Step 1: Hydrolysis of the nitrile.
Propanenitrile on basic hydrolysis followed by acidic workup gives propanoic acid:
$CH_3-CH_2-C \equiv N \xrightarrow[(ii)\ H_3O^+]{(i)\ OH^-/H_2O/\Delta} CH_3-CH_2-COOH$

Step 2: Hell$-$Volhard$-$Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction.
Propanoic acid has an $sp^3$ $\alpha$-carbon bearing two $\alpha$-hydrogens. In the HVZ reaction, $Cl_2$ in the presence of red phosphorus selectively replaces one $\alpha$-hydrogen by chlorine, giving the $\alpha$-chloro acid after aqueous workup:
$CH_3-CH_2-COOH \xrightarrow[(iv)\ H_2O]{(iii)\ Cl_2/\text{Red P}} CH_3-CH(Cl)-COOH$

Hence, the major product $P$ is $2$-chloropropanoic acid, which corresponds to option $(1)$.
topic: Preparation and Properties of Carboxylic Acids

question_text:
The descending order of acidity among the following compounds is:
A. Phenol
B. $4$-nitrophenol
C. $4$-methoxyphenol
D. $4$-nitrobenzoic acid
E. Benzoic acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution_text:
Carboxylic acids are stronger acids than phenols because the carboxylate anion is stabilized by equivalent resonance structures. Thus, D and E are more acidic than A, B, and C.

For the carboxylic acids, the $-NO_2$ group in D is an electron-withdrawing group ($-I, -R$), which stabilizes the conjugate base, making D more acidic than E.

For the phenols, electron-withdrawing groups increase acidity while electron-donating groups decrease it. The $-NO_2$ group in B is electron-withdrawing, making it more acidic than A. The $-OCH_3$ group in C is electron-donating ($+R > -I$), making it less acidic than A. Thus, the order for phenols is B $>$ A $>$ C.

Combining these, the overall descending order of acidity is D $>$ E $>$ B $>$ A $>$ C.

Answer: $D>E>B>A>C$
topic: Preparation and Properties of Carboxylic Acids

question_text:
The correct order of acidic strength of the major products formed in the given reactions, is :
A.
B. $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{CHO} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\right]^{+}, \mathrm{OH}^{-}}[\mathrm{B}]$
C. $\mathrm{CH}_{4}+\mathrm{O}_{2} \xrightarrow[\text { (ii) } \mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7} / \mathrm{H}^{+}]{\text {(i) }}[\mathrm{C}]$
D. $\mathrm{PhCH}_{2} \mathrm{MgBr}+\mathrm{CO}_{2} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H}_{3} \mathrm{O}^{+}]{\text {Dry ether }}[\mathrm{D}]$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution_text:
Product [A]: From PhNH₂, steps (1) NaNO₂ + HCl forms diazonium salt, (2) CuCN gives benzonitrile, (3) H₃O⁺/Δ hydrolyzes to benzoic acid (PhCOOH), pKa ≈ 4.2.
Product [B]: From CH₃CH₂CHO, Tollens' oxidation with $[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+$ produces acetic acid (CH₃COOH), pKa ≈ 4.8.
Product [C]: From CH₄ + O₂ with heat and Na₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺ produces formic acid (HCOOH), pKa ≈ 3.8 (strongest acid).
Product [D]: From PhCH₂MgBr + CO₂, the Grignard reaction produces phenylacetic acid (PhCH₂COOH), pKa ≈ 4.3.
Acidic strength order (lower pKa = stronger): C (3.8) > A (4.2) > D (4.3) > B (4.8).
topic: Preparation and Properties of Carboxylic Acids

question_text: Decarboxylation of all six possible forms of diaminobenzoic acids <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mfenced><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>COOH</mi></math> yields three products <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. Three acids give a product '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>', two acids gives a product '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>' and one acid give a product '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>'. The melting point of product '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>' is
solution_text:
C is a para isomer.

The melting point of para-isomer is comparatively higher than the corresponding  ortho and meta-isomers , because of more symmetrical nature; it fits into crystal lattice more readily and so, close packing of molecules in crystal lattice increases the intermolecular force of attraction between molecules.

Hence C has highest melting point that is 142 °C

question_text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mfenced></math> on treatment with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Br</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>FeBr</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CCl</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> produced a single isomer <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>8</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>Br</mi></math> wile heating <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mfenced></math> with sodalime gives toluene. The compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mfenced></math> is:
solution_text:
Isomer C8H7O2Br on heating with sodalime gives toluene,hence it is an acid.Moreover since it has Degree of unsaturation 5 therefore it is an aromatic carboxylic acid.Since Carboxylic acid on heating gives toluene ,therefore it is having -CH3 group attached to the benzene ring.

Now it forms single isomer on halogenation, therefore -CH3 group must be attached at para position with respect to -COOH group.

Hence correct option is 1.
